shared_inferential_jump: For each conservative-motion interval, select the actual system and build its appropriate potential from the forces and mass distribution, then fix E=K+U from a real state and use K=E−U≥0 to compare states or limit motion, with E=U marking zero-kinetic-energy candidates (actual turns require reversal) and the smallest accessible U marking greatest K (and greatest speed when mass or inertia is fixed).

question_to_jump_mapping.use: Restart the conservative-energy account after a sudden change of the applied force and compare two zero-speed points using the new effective potential.
Represent a changing height distribution by its centre-of-mass gravitational U and equate initial E to whole-chain final K+U.
Evaluate total E from rest, restrict the allowed x-domain, and find maximum K from minimum U by completing the square.

EXTENSION — BEYOND GRADE 9, GIVEN, parts (b),(c) only: horizontal release of intact rod reaches vertical, where it fractures without impulse; reselect the attached piece and apply its separately conserved rotational-and-gravitational ledger.

conventions.statement: State the physical system, the time interval, every included energy store, and the forces/transfers before equating K + U.
conventions.example: For a frictionless object and its conservative interaction, choose the system and interval; after a controlled force change write a new ledger.

conventions.statement: Choose a coordinate and signs: x to the right positive; vertical height h upward positive; angles measured from the vertically downward rest direction in the rotational extension.
conventions.example: A compressed spring is x < 0 and an extension is x > 0.

conventions.statement: Fix the same zero reference for gravitational/spring/effective potential at every compared position within an interval; adding the same constant to E and U changes no predictions.
conventions.example: For heights, U_g = mgh with zero at h=0; negative U is permitted.

conventions.statement: Restrict position to its physical domain, such as x>0 for a reciprocal potential, and to the interval actually connected to the initial position. Reject places where E < U.
conventions.example: A mathematical root on a disconnected island is not automatically reachable from the start.

conventions.statement: In the core, motion is along one coordinate with K=(1/2)mv², m>0; friction, impacts and unmodelled work are absent within each conserved interval.
conventions.example: Do not use K+U constant across a dissipative collision.

conventions.statement: At E=U, K=0; call a position a turning point only when the actual motion reaches it and reverses direction, not merely because a rest/equilibrium state satisfies the equality.
conventions.example: A bead released at rest at the bottom of a smooth bowl remains there in the ideal model and never reverses.

conventions.statement: For the rotation extension only: rotational kinetic energy K_rot=(1/2)Iω² and the appropriate moment of inertia are BEYOND GRADE 9, GIVEN, not derived here.
conventions.example: After a rod breaks at the vertical following release from horizontal, use the attached piece and its supplied I.

conventions.statement: WEP07-01 only: pre-reversal configuration is static spring equilibrium; after an instantaneous force reversal and doubling, assume an ideal Hooke spring, no damping or impulse, and a constant applied force on the new interval. Both U_s=kx²/2 and U_F=−Fx are SUPPLIED STRETCHES beyond baseline Grade 9.
conventions.example: An external field switch changes the interval energy model, not the instantaneous spring displacement.

conventions.statement: EXTENSION — BEYOND GRADE 9, GIVEN for WEP07-04(c): the rod starts from horizontal at rest and fractures without impulse exactly when passing vertical; evaluate the attached upper piece after that event.
conventions.example: The extension angle is conditional on that initial state and break geometry.

bucket.subject: Physics
bucket.stage: Grade 9 with explicitly marked rotational extension

microtopic.title: Use a conserved total to bound motion and locate genuine turning points
microtopic.badge_reason: Must build a closed energy account, translate nonnegative kinetic energy into spatial limits, distinguish zero speed from actual reversal, and handle model changes.
entry_assumptions: Can calculate translational kinetic energy (1/2)mv² and gravitational changes mgΔh.
Can identify conservative versus dissipative/external transfer before treating K+U as constant.
Can solve a simple quadratic inequality and complete a square without calculus.
Can choose a fixed energy reference and interpret a signed x coordinate.
Can distinguish an isolated stable-equilibrium rest state from a reached reversal by looking at motion before and after the instant.
Can compute the weighted mean height of two point masses; continuously distributed mass uses the same centre-of-mass idea as a stated bridge.
Can distinguish a force/field switching event from an impulse; in a no-impulse change the instantaneous speed remains continuous.
STRETCH beyond baseline Grade 9: accept U_s=kx²/2 and uniform-force U_F=−Fx as supplied conservative potentials, not newly derived Grade 9 laws.
ALGEBRA STRETCH: complete the square and, if WEP07-03 is attempted, treat z=x₀/x as a supplied optional substitution on x>0.
EXTENSION — BEYOND GRADE 9, GIVEN: rotational K=Iω²/2, moment of inertia, fixed-pivot model and impulse-free separation.
microtopic.inferential_jump: For each conservative-motion interval, select the actual system and build its appropriate potential from the forces and mass distribution, then fix E=K+U from a real state and use K=E−U≥0 to compare states or limit motion, with E=U marking zero-kinetic-energy candidates (actual turns require reversal) and the smallest accessible U marking greatest K (and greatest speed when mass or inertia is fixed).

teaching_path.action: Name the system and mark the particular interval whose energy is being compared.
teaching_path.why_valid: Otherwise an external force, fracture, or friction term may be omitted or double counted.

source_ref_binding.exact_concept: OpenStax 8.3 problem-solving strategy step 1: choose bodies/system and forces; canonical MIC-PHY-WEP-MECH-ENERGY-CONDITION.teaching_path WEP4-0

teaching_path.action: Choose an x-axis, potential-energy reference and physical domain before evaluating U(x).
teaching_path.why_valid: A potential value depends on the zero convention, while accessibility depends on consistent differences and a valid domain.

source_ref_binding.exact_concept: OpenStax 8.3 strategy step 4: select a potential reference for each conservative force; canonical MIC-PHY-WEP-GRADE9-QUANT.teaching_path WEP6-1

teaching_path.action: Test whether the chosen mechanical account is closed: only conservative interactions may exchange K and U, with no unaccounted work or dissipative transfer.
teaching_path.why_valid: The general energy law does not automatically imply K+U constant; this is exactly the canonical conservative-only condition.

teaching_path.action: Read initial speed and position; determine E = (1/2)mv_i² + U(x_i), or the matching total K plus U for the declared system.
teaching_path.why_valid: A fixed total must come from one genuine physical state, not an arbitrary guessed constant.

teaching_path.action: At any later accessible x, subtract: K(x)=E−U(x).
teaching_path.why_valid: Rearranging the conserved total E=K+U isolates the energy available for motion.

teaching_path.action: Reject any x with U(x)>E and retain connected allowed positions with U(x)≤E.
teaching_path.why_valid: Ordinary kinetic energy (1/2)mv² cannot be negative; non-negative algebra alone does not prove access across a forbidden gap.

teaching_path.action: At a reachable boundary where E=U, K=0 and speed is zero. Decide from the nearby allowed region and motion whether this is a reversal or merely a rest/equilibrium point.
teaching_path.why_valid: Equality is necessary for a zero-speed turning instant, but without adjacent admissible motion an isolated equilibrium need not reverse.

teaching_path.action: For a fixed positive mass, maximum speed is where K=E−U is greatest; equivalently where U is least among the reachable positions.
teaching_path.why_valid: The constant E does not depend on x; v²=2K/m grows with K.

teaching_path.action: Complete a quadratic square algebraically (do not differentiate) to locate the accessible potential minimum.
teaching_path.why_valid: A square is never negative, so the vertex form makes the least potential explicit.

source_ref_binding.exact_concept: Completing the square to rewrite a quadratic as squared binomial plus constant; the physics K_max inference is separately S08

teaching_path.action: For a collection of masses, sum each mgh or use total mass times centre-of-mass height; use a weighted position for unequal masses.
teaching_path.why_valid: Summing m_i g h_i equals (sum m_i)g h_cm under uniform g; this is the mass-weighted centre definition.

source_ref_binding.exact_concept: 9.6 centre-of-mass weighted-position definition; combined with canonical near-Earth gravitational mgh relation

teaching_path.action: When an externally controlled conservative field changes without impulse, carry physical x,v through the instant and compute a new U and E for the subsequent fixed-field interval.
teaching_path.why_valid: One time-independent potential and total apply only within the interval under the stated unchanged forces; the switching event may exchange energy externally.

source_ref_binding.exact_concept: OpenStax 8.3 conservative-only interval condition; event matching of x,v is an explicitly assumed no-impulse model, not claimed verbatim from the source

teaching_path.action: EXTENSION — BEYOND GRADE 9, GIVEN: if a rotating rod fractures at the vertical after horizontal release and without impulse, reselect the attached fragment and its inertia for the post-fracture energy ledger.
teaching_path.why_valid: The attached piece has a different mass distribution and rotational inertia; do not apply the intact-rod total to the selected fragment.

source_ref_binding.exact_concept: Rotational K and moment of inertia relation; breakup at vertical/no impulse is a problem-specific supplied assumption, not a published general OpenStax result

teaching_path.action: For rotational motion only, insert the GIVEN beyond-Grade-9 relation K_rot=(1/2)Iω², then use E=K_rot+U and K_rot=0 at an angular turning point.
teaching_path.why_valid: Changing K from translation to rotation does not change the allowed-energy inference; the rotational relation is an advanced prerequisite.

teaching_path.action: Check units, limits, sign of K, reference-offset invariance, and whether alleged turning positions can actually be reached from the stated start.
teaching_path.why_valid: An algebraically consistent root can still violate physical domain, state continuity or the conditions of conservation.

misconceptions.wrong_idea: Energy is always conserved, therefore K + U is always unchanged.
misconceptions.diagnostic_prompt: A puck slides across a rough patch and warms it; can its translational K plus gravitational U remain constant without a friction-transfer term?
misconceptions.diagnostic_answer: No; energy transfers to internal/thermal stores.
misconceptions.repair: Write a system/store/transfer ledger first; use unchanged K+U only after a zero-extra-transfer check.

misconceptions.wrong_idea: If U is negative, total energy or K must also be negative.
misconceptions.diagnostic_prompt: If E=0 and U=−3 J at one permitted position, what is K?
misconceptions.diagnostic_answer: K=3 J; negative potential relative to a chosen reference is allowed.
misconceptions.repair: Use K=E−U and test K≥0, not the sign of U alone.

misconceptions.wrong_idea: Every solution of E=U is a reached turning point, and E=U always implies reversal.
misconceptions.diagnostic_prompt: An object sits at rest in a stable equilibrium and remains there. Is it reversing direction every instant?
misconceptions.diagnostic_answer: No; E=U but there is no incoming/outgoing motion to reverse.
misconceptions.repair: Examine the physical domain, connection to the initial state and accessible sides near the zero-speed position.

misconceptions.wrong_idea: Maximum speed occurs where potential U is maximum.
misconceptions.diagnostic_prompt: At E=10 J, compare the speeds where U=2 J and U=8 J for the same moving mass.
misconceptions.diagnostic_answer: Faster at U=2 J, where K=8 J instead of 2 J.
misconceptions.repair: Calculate K=E−U before comparing speed, then compare smallest accessible U.

misconceptions.wrong_idea: After a controlled force switch, the old energy model stays valid; EXTENSION — BEYOND GRADE 9, GIVEN: after a rod fracture the intact body and its inertia still apply.
misconceptions.diagnostic_prompt: GRADE 9: when a uniform conservative field is switched off without impulse, should its previous U still be used? EXTENSION — BEYOND GRADE 9, GIVEN: after a rod fractures at vertical, can the intact I be used for the attached fragment?
misconceptions.diagnostic_answer: No to both; reconstruct the active interval model; EXTENSION — BEYOND GRADE 9, GIVEN: reconstruct the post-fracture subsystem and I.
misconceptions.repair: Separate the intervals by a force-switch marker; EXTENSION — BEYOND GRADE 9, GIVEN: for fracture, additionally specify the attached rotating fragment and supplied inertia.

misconceptions.wrong_idea: All of a chain has the same gravitational potential per unit length as the hanging tip.
misconceptions.diagnostic_prompt: A vertical uniform length y has midpoint at depth y/2; should its total gravitational U be based on tip depth y or centre depth y/2?
misconceptions.diagnostic_answer: Use centre depth y/2 and the mass of the hanging portion.
misconceptions.repair: Write mass λy, then centre height −y/2, then multiply before mixing in whole-chain K.

exit_task.prompt: With U(x)=(x−1)² J and E=4 J on a frictionless 1D track (x in metres), give the allowed interval, the potential minimum and speed-maximum position, and which E=U points represent turns for a moving cart.

answer.summary: Allowed −1≤x≤3 m; U_min=0 J at x=1 m, where speed is greatest; the boundaries x=−1 m and x=3 m are turns if the moving cart reaches and reverses at them.
reasoning: K is largest when the square is smallest: x=1.
At each end K=0; the motion/reversal check distinguishes a turn from a static rest.
answer.check: Try x=4: U=9 J>4 J, so K would be −5 J and it is forbidden. Try x=1: K=4 J≥0.

microtopic.research_contribution: Adapted the already-canonical conditional-mechanical-energy ledger to an explicitly proposed turning-point construction; enrichment verified against OpenStax University Physics 8.3 and 8.4. No calculus, and the original exam corpus is not used as conceptual authority.

predict.prompt: A frictionless cart has E=4 J and a position-dependent potential U(x)=(x−1)² J, with x in metres. Before calculating a trajectory, can it ever occupy x=4 m? Where should it move fastest?
predict.defensible_answer: No: U(4)=9 J exceeds E=4 J. Speed is largest at x=1 m, where U is smallest.

attempt.produces: Without seeing the model response, draw the x-axis and an energy-line sketch, write K(x), solve the allowed x interval, label zero-speed candidate boundaries, locate the fastest position and explain one reason E=U may fail to mean reversal.
attempt.model_response: K(x)=4−(x−1)² J. K≥0 gives −1≤x≤3 m. x=−1 and x=3 are zero-speed boundaries; for a cart moving inside that connected interval they are turning positions. The minimum U is 0 J at x=1, so K_max=4 J there. A cart that starts exactly at a stable equilibrium with zero speed can remain there with K=0 and never reverse; no person or holding force is needed.

rubric.criterion: Declare system, coordinate, physical domain and zero-extra-transfer assumption.
rubric.evidence_of: A statement tying conservation to a frictionless, unchanged model.
Subtract U from E before solving.
Both square-root inequality boundaries and exclusion.

rubric.criterion: Separate candidate equality points from actual reversals.
Place K maximum where U minimum: x=1.

accepted: For a moving cart within −1 to 3 m, it turns at the two ends and moves fastest at 1 m.
E=U flags a rest location, but no reversal occurs if it simply stays in equilibrium.
rejected: x=4 is allowed because potential can be greater than total energy.
Speed is greatest at either turning boundary.
Any rest position automatically means an actual reversal.

route.ask: What physically defined system and interval make E constant here?
route.why_this_ask: Conservation is earned by verifying its condition, not assumed merely from the presence of U.
route.model_answer: Frictionless cart plus conservative interaction during one fixed-potential interval.

route.ask: What must be nonnegative at every real position?
route.why_this_ask: This selects the constraint that distinguishes a physical path from an algebraically imaginable coordinate.

route.ask: How do you turn the constraint into a marked segment on an x-axis?
route.why_this_ask: Translates energy arithmetic into spatial accessibility.

route.ask: If the kinetic bar vanishes at one end, what extra observation makes it a turning point?
route.why_this_ask: Distinguishes equality from actual reversal or equilibrium.
route.model_answer: A moving trajectory reaches the boundary and changes direction, rather than remaining motionless.

route.ask: Where is E−U largest on that segment?
route.why_this_ask: Extracts maximum speed by minimising U, not by confusing it with maximum potential.
route.model_answer: At x=1, where U=(x−1)² is zero.

route.ask: GRADE 9 reset: If an external conservative field is switched off without impulse, which measured state quantities persist, and which interval energy ledger must you construct anew?
route.why_this_ask: Rebuilds the event-reset condition rather than blindly reusing the earlier total.
route.model_answer: Position and velocity carry through a no-impulse force switch; rebuild U and E for the post-switch interval. EXTENSION — BEYOND GRADE 9: if a rod fractures, also reselect the physical subsystem and the supplied inertia.

route.ask: A chain segment hangs y below the edge. Which height represents the whole hanging segment?
route.why_this_ask: Makes the learner construct the distributed gravitational ledger before applying energy conservation.
route.model_answer: Its centre-of-mass height −y/2; the segment has mass λy.

route.ask: On −4≤q≤0, U(q)=q²+4q+9 J and E=9 J: which constant completes the square, and where is K largest?
route.why_this_ask: Requires constructing the algebraic vertex in the original coordinate rather than repeating the reciprocal-potential substitution of WEP07-03.
route.model_answer: U=(q+2)²+5, so K=4−(q+2)² reaches 4 J at q=−2, without calculus.

route.ask: EXTENSION — BEYOND GRADE 9, GIVEN: after a flywheel’s attached bead detaches, which inertia and subsystem belong to the next interval?
route.why_this_ask: Keeps the extension at the same core inference while marking advanced mechanics as supplied.
route.model_answer: Use the flywheel-only system with its supplied inertia, not the combined pre-detachment inertia.

reconstruct.differs_from_teaching_path: CORE1A directly builds from system declarations to the energy inequality and then applies cases. CORE1B opens with an unfamiliar shifted potential and a commitment about a forbidden point, makes the learner produce a diagram/domain before any reveal, then reconstructs from the physical impossibility of negative kinetic energy and only later tests model resets, distributed mass, algebra and given rotation.

boundary_test.prompt: Two frictionless beads have zero speed at the same instant. Bead A reaches the rim of a smooth bowl while moving outward, then travels back inward; bead B is released exactly at rest at the bowl bottom and stays there. In which case is that instant a turning point? If a zero-speed bead is at the end of a downhill ramp with unlimited length ahead, must there be a second turn? Justify using motion on either side of the instant, not only an energy equality.
boundary_test.answer: Bead A reverses at its reached rim and has a genuine turning instant. Bead B is in stable equilibrium without incoming/outgoing motion and has no turn. On an indefinitely descending frictionless ramp an initially stationary bead can accelerate downhill continually and have no second turning point; a zero-speed event alone does not imply a later reversal.
boundary_test.confirms: Tests the missing assumptions: actual incoming/reversing motion, equilibrium rest, connected domain and lack of an enclosing second boundary.

relation.equation: E=K+U(x); K=E−U(x)≥0; E=U(x) at a zero-speed candidate boundary
model_assumptions: chosen consistent physical system and energy reference
only conservative transfers within fixed interval
physical domain and trajectory connectivity accounted for
relation.dimensions: K, E, U in joules; x in metres; (1/2)mv² in joules
relation.physical_interpretation: Potential higher than E is inaccessible; reached equality may identify a turning position if reversal is present.

checks.action: At any permitted x, recompute K+U and verify it equals the E from the same interval.
checks.expected: No drift of E within a conserved interval.

checks.action: Test the edges E=U and one point beyond with U>E.
checks.expected: K=0 at the edge, negative K and hence forbidden just beyond.

checks.action: Add a constant C to all U values and to E; re-evaluate E−U.
checks.expected: The allowed set and speeds do not change.

checks.action: In a potential with a genuine minimum, compare speeds at the minimum and at a turning boundary.
checks.expected: Speed maximal at U minimum and zero at a reached turning boundary.

checks.action: For a hanging chain, let initial hanging length approach the full chain length.
checks.expected: If the chain starts already fully hanging and at rest, its final speed from the same-state comparison tends to zero.

checks.action: At the fracture/force-change event, write left and right energy ledgers separately.
checks.expected: They share the actual instantaneous state; they need not share the same U model or the same system energy total.

checks.action: Compare an actual moving bead that reverses at a bowl rim with one that is initially at rest in stable equilibrium at the bottom.
checks.expected: Both can have E=U instantaneously, but only the moving bead reverses.

checks.action: For a uniform downhill conservative force along an ideal infinite ramp, test whether K returns to zero for any s>0 when released at rest at s=0.
checks.expected: No. K increases as s grows, so no second finite turn is forced.

correspondence.element: horizontal line E=9 J in SCN01 / total height of each bar row SCN02
correspondence.in_words: One fixed total chosen from the initial state.
correspondence.forward: The horizontal line represents the same energy at every position.
correspondence.reverse: An unchanged total bar height means the same E line throughout.

correspondence.element: parabola height in SCN01 / potential part of bars in SCN02
correspondence.in_words: Position-dependent energy stored in the conservative interaction.
correspondence.forward: Read a curve height at x as U.
correspondence.reverse: A potential bar value locates the height on the U curve.

correspondence.element: vertical separation between line and curve / kinetic part of bar
correspondence.in_words: Energy left for movement after potential is accounted for.
correspondence.forward: Positive line-above-curve gap is kinetic energy.
correspondence.reverse: Bar kinetic height gives the graph’s line-to-curve gap.

correspondence.element: line/curve contact or intersection in SCN01 / K=0 bar in SCN02
correspondence.in_words: Zero-speed candidate boundary that requires a reachability and reversal test.
correspondence.forward: Intersection makes the kinetic bar vanish.
correspondence.reverse: Zero kinetic bar corresponds to an equality point, not automatically a reversal.

correspondence.element: curve above E line / no physical K bar
correspondence.in_words: Forbidden position for the chosen fixed energy.
correspondence.forward: Above-line positions demand negative kinetic energy.
correspondence.reverse: An impossible negative bar shows the point must be excluded.

correspondence.element: two differently weighted points and COM dot in SCN04
correspondence.in_words: For several bodies, total gravitational potential uses each mass’s height or their mass-weighted mean height.
correspondence.forward: Weight heights by their masses before constructing total U.
correspondence.reverse: The COM dot at 2.5 m encodes the weighted total of unequal masses.

correspondence.element: rotating piece speed marker in SCN05
correspondence.in_words: Given beyond-Grade-9 rotational kinetic energy replaces translational K.
correspondence.forward: At ω=0, K_rot=0 and energy is potential.
correspondence.reverse: The rotating speed marker is not a linear v and needs the given I formula.

correspondence.element: gap between E=0 line and declining U in SCN06
correspondence.in_words: Moving downhill can keep gaining kinetic energy without another zero-speed position.
correspondence.forward: The gap increases forever in the ideal domain.
correspondence.reverse: No second intersection means no second finite turn is forced by energy.

correspondence.element: two side-by-side energy ledgers in SCN07
correspondence.in_words: The same instantaneous speed can lead to different interval energy numbers after a controlled force change.
correspondence.forward: Compute each E using the potential active on its side.
correspondence.reverse: Different ledger totals do not mean the cart speed jumped.

correspondence.element: two temporal motion strips in SCN08
correspondence.in_words: An actual direction reversal requires incoming and outgoing motion; rest equilibrium does not turn.
correspondence.forward: Inspect events before and after zero speed.
correspondence.reverse: A static bead cannot be called an oscillation turning point.

questions.title: Read a U(x) picture as a motion boundary
questions.setup: A frictionless 1D cart of positive mass has U(x)=x² J for x in metres, with coefficient 1 J/m². From its known initial state E=9 J. Identify physically allowed x, reached turn boundaries for a cart moving between them, and x of maximum speed.

reasoning: The system is the cart and conservative interaction; friction is absent. The potential reference and x coordinate are fixed.
Conservation gives K(x)=9−x² J. K cannot be negative.
The allowed inequality 9−x²≥0 implies −3≤x≤3 metres.
At x=−3 and +3, K=0. For a cart travelling within the interval and reversing at each boundary, these are the turning positions.
The smallest U in the allowed interval is 0 J at x=0, so K is maximal there at 9 J. No mass value is required to locate where speed is maximal.
answer.summary: Allowed interval −3≤x≤3 m; turning boundaries −3 m and +3 m for the moving cart; maximum speed at x=0.
answer.check: K(−3)=K(3)=0; K(0)=9 J; K(4)=−7 J is inadmissible.

questions.title: A moving cart crosses a field switch without an impulse
questions.setup: A 2 kg cart is travelling at 3 m/s when a uniform conservative driving field is switched OFF at x=2 m on an infinite horizontal frictionless track. Before switching, the field potential is U_A(x)=−(2 J/m)x; after switching U_B=0. Compare the energy ledger immediately on either side of the event and the subsequent motion.

reasoning: Use the same actual event state x=2 m and v=3 m/s immediately before/after because switching is assumed impulse-free.
K=mv²/2=(1/2)(2)(3²)=9 J at the event.
Before the switch U_A(2)=−4 J, giving old interval total E_A=9−4=5 J.
After the switch there is no field, U_B=0, and the post-switch interval E_B=9+0=9 J. The two totals need not have the same numerical value because the model changed at the controlled switching event.
In the new force-free interval K remains 9 J and motion continues with constant speed; there is no finite second turning point.
answer.summary: No impulse gives unchanged speed; the post-switch mechanical ledger has E_B=9 J and no finite turning point.
answer.check: K=9 J on both event sides; old E_A=5 J, new E_B=9 J. No discontinuous change of the measured speed is asserted.

questions.title: Mass-weighted height for two connected unequal masses
questions.setup: A rigid light carrier keeps two small masses vertically aligned: 1 kg at height 1 m and 3 kg at height 3 m; both descend together by 0.5 m from rest on frictionless guides (g=10 m/s²). Calculate their combined initial centre-of-mass height, their gravitational energy change and their total kinetic energy gain.

reasoning: Choose both masses and Earth, with h upward and zero at h=0; the light carrier’s kinetic energy is neglected.
The initial mass-weighted centre height is (1 kg×1 m+3 kg×3 m)/(4 kg)=2.5 m, not the unweighted midpoint 2 m.
Both masses descend 0.5 m, so the final heights are 0.5 and 2.5 m and their centre height becomes 2.0 m.
The gravitational potential change is M g Δh_cm=4×10×(−0.5)=−20 J; summing separate mgh changes gives the same −20 J.
In the absence of extra work, K_total rises by 20 J; because they share one speed, K_total=(1/2)(4 kg)v².
answer.summary: Initial centre height 2.5 m; ΔU=−20 J; K gain 20 J for the two-mass system.
answer.check: Individual changes −5 J and −15 J sum to −20 J. COM weighting, not simple midpoint, is decisive.

questions.title: Minimum potential by completing the square
questions.setup: For an abstract position coordinate z restricted to 0≤z≤4, U(z)=2(z−2)²−8 J and E=0. Find the allowed range and the maximum kinetic energy, using algebra only.

reasoning: Conservation gives K=E−U=8−2(z−2)² J.
K≥0 requires (z−2)²≤4, which agrees with 0≤z≤4.
The square (z−2)² is never negative, and is least (zero) at z=2.
Thus U is least at z=2, where U=−8 J, and K is greatest at 8 J.
At the boundaries z=0 and z=4, U=0=E and K=0. Negative U is not a problem because kinetic energy stays nonnegative.
answer.summary: Maximum K=8 J at z=2, with zero-speed boundaries z=0 and z=4.
answer.check: K(0)=0, K(2)=8 J and K(4)=0; at z=5, K=−10 J so that location would be forbidden if included in the domain.

questions.title: EXTENSION: a rotating system obeys the same zero-speed energy test
questions.setup: BEYOND GRADE 9, GIVEN: a rigid piece rotates around a fixed hinge with moment of inertia I=2 kg·m². At its lowest configuration it has angular speed ω=3 rad/s and mass m=1 kg; take g=10 m/s². Assuming no loss or external work afterwards, find the centre-of-mass rise achievable by using up its rotational kinetic energy.

reasoning: The rotating piece and Earth are the declared system after the event; no friction or drive acts.
Use the GIVEN beyond-Grade-9 formula K_rot=(1/2)Iω², so the initial K_rot=0.5×2×3²=9 J.
At an angular turning position ω=0 and rotational K is zero.
The centre of mass must gain gravitational U=m g Δh=9 J, so Δh=9/(1×10)=0.9 m.
This energy comparison predicts a maximum rise only if the geometry of the actual hinged piece permits that height; otherwise its allowed geometry is the restricting condition.
answer.summary: Conditional energy-based centre-of-mass rise Δh=0.9 m; geometric reachability must still be checked.
answer.check: Iω² has joule units and mgΔh=9 J. The formula for I and K_rot is supplied, not derived.

questions.title: An indefinitely descending path has no second turning point
questions.setup: An ideal frictionless bead starts from rest at position s=0 on an indefinitely long descending straight ramp. Take the downhill position s≥0, and suppose U(s)=−(2 J/m)s. Describe the allowed positions, kinetic energy and whether a second finite turning point exists.

reasoning: Declare bead-plus-Earth and a fixed downhill coordinate s≥0; uniform gravity along the ramp is conservative and no friction acts.
At s=0 the bead rests and U(0)=0, so E=0.
At any s≥0, K(s)=E−U(s)=(2 J/m)s, which is nonnegative and grows without bound in the ideal infinite-ramp model.
The starting point s=0 is a zero-speed boundary, but a release from rest followed by motion downhill is not a reversal there.
There is no further finite root K=0 for s>0, so there is no second turning point and no finite maximum speed in this unbounded idealisation.
answer.summary: Allowed domain s≥0, K=2s J for s in metres, no second finite turning point.
answer.check: At s=1 m, K=2 J; at s=10 m, K=20 J; K does not return to zero for s>0.

predict.prompt: A 2 kg cart passes x=2 m at 3 m/s on a level frictionless track when a uniform driving field is switched OFF without an impulse; before the switch the field potential was U_A(x)=−(2 J/m)x. Can you keep using the old potential after switch-off?
predict.defensible_answer: No. Its x and v at the event are unchanged, but the post-switch field is absent; use U_B=0 and compute a new interval total.

attempt.produces: Draw a two-column energy ledger immediately before and after the switch. Identify what carries through unchanged and compute both interval totals; do not invent a turning point.
attempt.model_response: K=0.5(2)(3²)=9 J at the event. Before: U_A(2)=−4 J, E_A=5 J. After: U_B=0, E_B=9 J; cart coasts with K=9 J, no new turn on the infinite level track. The before/after totals refer to different potential models, not a violation of energy conservation.

rubric.criterion: States no impulse: x=2 m and v=3 m/s unchanged at switch.
rubric.evidence_of: Distinguishes instantaneous state from energy-model bookkeeping.

rubric.criterion: Computes both totals under their respective models.
rubric.evidence_of: Before 5 J; after 9 J with K=9 J.
Does not force E_A=E_B or claim a post-switch turn.

accepted: At the switch, the physical speed stays 3 m/s and the force-free interval has E=9 J.
rejected: The earlier −2x potential remains after the force is removed.

route.ask: Does a force-switch without impulse instantly change v?
route.why_this_ask: Keeps actual state separate from the model.
route.model_answer: No.

route.ask: Which of the two potential formulas belongs to each interval?
route.why_this_ask: Rebuilds the conservation condition.
route.model_answer: U_A=−2x J before; U_B=0 after.

route.ask: Why may two interval totals differ as numbers?
route.why_this_ask: Avoids using one changed potential reference as if unchanged.
route.model_answer: They are different energy ledgers; force switching is an external event.

reconstruct.differs_from_teaching_path: Learner must first reject persistence of the switched-off field, then construct two actual-state ledgers.

boundary_test.prompt: If the field is switched off when v=0 instead, does turning follow solely from K=0?
boundary_test.answer: No; the force-free cart can remain at rest, with no reversal.
boundary_test.confirms: Zero speed does not itself imply a turn.

predict.prompt: A light rigid carrier holds 1 kg at height 1 m and 3 kg at height 3 m. If both move down together by 0.5 m with no friction, is their combined gravitational energy change found using the simple midpoint 2 m?
predict.defensible_answer: No. Use a mass-weighted centre height (2.5 m initially) or sum each mass’s mgh; the total change is −20 J for g=10 m/s².

attempt.produces: Calculate mass-weighted centre height before and after, total gravitational potential change, and the resulting combined kinetic energy if released from rest.
attempt.model_response: The centre height is (1×1+3×3)/4=2.5 m initially and (1×0.5+3×2.5)/4=2.0 m finally. ΔU=4×10×(−0.5)=−20 J; total kinetic energy gained is 20 J. Both parts move together, so K=(1/2)(4)v².

rubric.criterion: Uses mass weighting, not the ordinary unweighted mean.
Computes ΔU using mass and change in centre height.
rubric.evidence_of: ΔU=−20 J, or same from separate masses.

rubric.criterion: Includes the entire moving mass in K.

accepted: Compute separate mgh changes (−5 J and −15 J) to get −20 J.
rejected: Use midpoint 2 m as the initial centre despite unequal masses.

route.ask: Which object contributes more to the centre position?
route.why_this_ask: Makes the learner build a weighted position, not repeat a chain formula.
route.model_answer: The 3 kg object has triple the weight in the average.

route.ask: How does changing each height by the same amount shift the weighted centre?
route.why_this_ask: Connects geometric motion to U change.
route.model_answer: The centre also shifts down by 0.5 m.

route.ask: Whose speed belongs in K after release?
route.why_this_ask: Avoids losing part of the system.
route.model_answer: Both masses, with the same carrier speed.

reconstruct.differs_from_teaching_path: Builds energy for two unequal point masses, not a continuously distributed chain.

boundary_test.prompt: If the 3 kg mass is doubled while the vertical shifts stay 0.5 m, what remains unchanged and what changes?
boundary_test.answer: The centre still drops 0.5 m; combined mass becomes 7 kg, so |ΔU| becomes 35 J for g=10 m/s².
boundary_test.confirms: Distinguishes geometric shift from total-mass weighting.

predict.prompt: For a positive-mass frictionless particle on −4≤q≤0, let U(q)=q²+4q+9 J and E=9 J. Must the greatest speed occur at q=0, or could it occur inside the interval?
predict.defensible_answer: It occurs inside: rewriting U=(q+2)²+5 makes its minimum at q=−2, hence K maximum there.

attempt.produces: Complete the square by adding and subtracting a constant, identify the accessible domain and find the position and value of K_max without differentiation.
attempt.model_response: q²+4q+9=(q+2)²+5 J; K=9−U=4−(q+2)² J. K≥0 implies −4≤q≤0, matching the stated interval. At q=−2, K_max=4 J; at both endpoints K=0.

rubric.criterion: Identifies minimum U and maximum K using square≥0.
rubric.evidence_of: q=−2, K_max=4 J with no calculus.

rejected: Greatest speed is at the highest U or the right endpoint.

route.ask: Which constant completes q²+4q into a square?
route.why_this_ask: Needs algebraic choice rather than supplied pattern.

route.ask: What does the completed square tell you about minimum U?
route.why_this_ask: Builds the minimum without calculus.
route.model_answer: It is 5 J at q=−2.

route.ask: How do you get maximum K for fixed E?
route.why_this_ask: Links algebra to physics.
route.model_answer: Subtract the smallest U from 9 J.

reconstruct.differs_from_teaching_path: Learner chooses a square-completion constant for an expanded quadratic with a negative-coordinate domain, not the reciprocal substitution from the exam.

boundary_test.prompt: If E is lowered to 4 J with this U, can the particle occupy any point?
boundary_test.answer: No: U≥5 J everywhere, so K=E−U<0 throughout.
boundary_test.confirms: An algebraic energy value must permit some nonnegative K before motion exists.

predict.prompt: EXTENSION — BEYOND GRADE 9, GIVEN: a flywheel and a bead are coupled, then the bead detaches without impulse. Can the flywheel’s later kinetic energy be calculated by keeping the old combined inertia?
predict.defensible_answer: No. After separation, choose the flywheel alone; use its own GIVEN moment of inertia and angular speed to form the new ledger.

attempt.produces: Mark before/after subsystem boundaries. With GIVEN I_flywheel=1 kg·m², ω=2 rad/s at separation and no further work, compute the flywheel’s post-event rotational kinetic energy and explain why its own energy ledger is required.
attempt.model_response: EXTENSION — BEYOND GRADE 9, GIVEN: K_rot=(1/2)Iω²=(1/2)(1)(2²)=2 J for the flywheel alone. The old combined system has different inertia and may have shared energy; it is not the post-event flywheel total.

rubric.criterion: Explicitly selects the flywheel-only post-detachment system.
Treats K_rot formula and I as GIVEN beyond Grade 9.
rubric.evidence_of: Uses 0.5 Iω² without deriving rotational dynamics.

rubric.criterion: Computes 2 J and marks the new interval.
rubric.evidence_of: 2 J post-event rotational K, with no automatic identity to old full-system E.

accepted: Flywheel-only kinetic energy is 2 J after detachment.
rejected: Use the old inertia for the detached flywheel.

route.ask: What changed at the detachment?
route.why_this_ask: Forces explicit subsystem selection.
route.model_answer: The original combined body split; only the flywheel remains.

route.ask: Which inertia belongs to the flywheel-only interval?
route.why_this_ask: Stops accidental reuse of whole-system inertia.
route.model_answer: The GIVEN flywheel I=1 kg·m².

route.ask: What can energy conservation then say in a later loss-free interval?
route.why_this_ask: Transfers the same invariant to the new system.
route.model_answer: Flywheel K_rot+its U remains constant for that interval if no transfer.

reconstruct.differs_from_teaching_path: An object-detachment comparison replaces the original hinged-rod turning-angle route.

boundary_test.prompt: If an external brake acts after detachment, is the flywheel K_rot necessarily conserved?
boundary_test.answer: No. The brake transfers energy out of its rotational mechanical store.
boundary_test.confirms: Rotation does not remove the conservative-interval condition.

concept_model_selection.evidence: Select a post-reversal effective potential for spring plus applied constant force, rather than spring potential alone.

representation_translation.evidence: Convert compression and extension into signed positions x = −ξ and x > 0.

reasoning_chain_length.evidence: First infer kξ=F, then set the post-switch conserved energy, then locate the other rest position.

algebra_computational_load.evidence: Expand and factor a quadratic in x/ξ.

hint_ladder_authored_not_source: Decide what happens to the conserved energy expression immediately after the force changes.
Measure x from natural length; compression and extension have opposite signs.
At the extreme extension, speed is again zero; compare the total potential at the two rest points.

reasoning_route.description: At the initial equilibrium the original force gives F=kξ.
Choose x positive along the new applied force, so the initial coordinate is −ξ; after switching, U_eff(x)=kx²/2−2Fx.
Immediately after switching the spring is still at −ξ with zero speed: E= kξ²/2+2Fξ=5kξ²/2.
At an extreme extension K=0, hence kx²/2−2kξx=5kξ²/2.
Thus x²−4ξx−5ξ²=(x−5ξ)(x+ξ)=0; exclude the already-known initial root x=−ξ.
The other turning point is x=5ξ, choice d.

The applied force reverses direction and doubles instantaneously; no impulsive jump in speed/displacement.
Ideal Hooke spring, no damping/friction; the NEW applied force is constant after switching.
SUPPLIED STRETCH: U_s=kx²/2 and uniform-force potential −Fx (rather than a baseline Grade 9 derivation).

representation_translation.evidence: Translate changing dangling length into gravitational energy of a uniform segment at centre-of-mass depth y/2.

reasoning_chain_length.evidence: Form U_initial and U_final, calculate their difference, and equate to whole-chain kinetic energy.

hint_ladder_authored_not_source: Use the tabletop edge as zero gravitational height.
At a hanging length y, determine the hanging mass and its centre-of-mass depth.
For kinetic energy, remember the entire chain is moving when it leaves the table.

reasoning_route.description: When length y hangs, that portion has mass λy and mean gravitational height −y/2; therefore U(y)=−λgy²/2.
The initial energy is E_i=−λgy₀²/2 because the chain is released from rest.
Just before leaving the edge, U_f=−λgL²/2 and K_f=(λL)v²/2.
Set E_i=U_f+K_f and cancel λ/2.
Obtain Lv²=g(L²−y₀²), hence v=√[g(L−y₀²/L)], choice a.

s2_question_support_retained_with_s3_rev.uses_jump: Evaluate total E from rest, restrict the allowed x-domain, and find maximum K from minimum U by completing the square.

concept_model_selection.evidence: Apply a single conserved energy to all four statements, identifying E=U(x₀)=0.

representation_translation.evidence: Introduce dimensionless z=x₀/x and preserve the admissible interval 0≤z≤1 implied by E≥U.

reasoning_chain_length.evidence: Coordinate potential rescaling, energy conservation, velocity expression, domain and maximum-speed evaluation.

algebra_computational_load.evidence: Symbolically substitute β=α/x₀, solve for square-root velocity and complete a square to maximise z−z².

trap_exception_sensitivity.evidence: A positive kinetic energy coexists with E=0 because U can be negative; the x-domain cannot be ignored.

hint_ladder_authored_not_source: Find the starting value of potential energy before writing the speed formula.
Express U in terms of the dimensionless ratio x₀/x.
A quadratic of the form z−z² has a maximum that can be found by completing the square.

reasoning_route.description: Since x₀=α/β, write β=α/x₀ and U(x)=α/x₀²[(x₀/x)²−x₀/x].
At the release point x=x₀, U(x₀)=0 and K=0; thus the conserved total energy E=0.
Hence K(x)=−U(x)=α/x₀²[z−z²] where z=x₀/x, and v(x)=√{2α/[mx₀²]·[z−z²]}.
The accessible outward branch has x≥x₀ and thus 0<z≤1; x₀ is its finite turning point and no smaller positive x is accessible.
Complete the square z−z²=1/4−(z−1/2)²; its maximum 1/4 occurs at z=1/2 or x=2x₀.
Then v_max²=α/(2mx₀²). Claims a, b, c and d all hold.

reasoning_route.description: Let total rod mass be M. From horizontal rest, its COM descends L/2; equate MgL/2=(1/2)(ML²/3)ω².

At the break its kinetic energy about O is (1/2)I_topω²=MgL/16.
When the upper piece reaches a turning angle θ, K=0 and its COM rises by (L/4)(1−cosθ). Set MgL/16=(MgL/8)(1−cosθ), obtaining θ=60°; this confirms c under the horizontal-release state.
